notes:
Top-line: product analytics SaaS building customer-facing ‘ask my data’ and support summarization. Started on Redwood Hosted API; now evaluating Dedicated for predictability and lower unit cost.

Trial observations (hosted):
- Typical session: user prompt ~100-180 tokens, average completion ~220 tokens.
- Token mix: ~65% short answers (<150 tokens), ~25% medium (150-600 tokens), ~10% long (600+ tokens).
- Workload split: chat (60%), semantic search (25%), reranking (15%).
- Observed avg QPS (week of 2026-02-22): baseline 6-8 QPS, peak bursts to 22 QPS (10:00–11:00 PST).
- Measured concurrency: typical 4-8 concurrent streams, p95 concurrency ~18 during burst window.
- p95 latency on Hosted p50=90ms, p95=140ms (for configured model llm-13b-quant), embeddings requests p95=45ms.
- Token spend during trial: ~$4.6k credits used (2 week window).

Dedicated ask / sizing constraints:
- Wants reserved capacity to sustain 20 QPS steady for chat + search with headroom for 40 QPS peaks for marketing events.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability, p95 latency target <= 200ms for chat generation at 1k token horizons.
- Concurrency planning: estimate 30 active worker threads at peak (based on session multiplexing), want concurrency buffer + autoscale.
- Model preference: prefer a quantized 13B variant (best cost/latency trade) but needs option to fallback to a 70B variant for high-fidelity summaries.
- Routing policy: prefer region-aware routing (NA primary, EU failover), fallback to cheaper model variant during capacity pressure.

POC notes / engineering feedback:
- CloudOps: will deploy VPC peering to Redwood Private network; need network diagram and egress IPs (asked 2026-02-28).
- SE feedback (Ravi): batching helps significantly for short queries; recommended batch size 8-12 for reranking path.
- Observed caching opportunity: 12% of requests identical prefixes -> candidate for prefix/KV caching.
- Quantization concerns: dev ML team wants benchmark on hallucination rate vs 13B-quant before committing.

Commercial / procurement:
- Finance asking for committed monthly GPU hours and unit pricing per 1M tokens. Requesting three tier options: small (20 QPS reserve), medium (40 QPS reserve), large (burst + DR).
- Wants clear migration path from Hosted credits to Dedicated commit.

Direct quotes / paraphrases from contact (CTO Anika Rao):
- "We need predictable unit economics — if we can get stable pricing at scale, this is a no-brainer."
- "Latency spikes during peak demo days are unacceptable; we need headroom and autoscale policies."

Next steps (short):
- Deliver Dedicated sizing spreadsheet with assumptions: observed QPS, token mix, average sequence length, concurrent sessions, cache hit rate. (Owner: Ravi)
- Provide infra/VPC diagram and egress IP list (Owner: CloudOps docs, due 2026-03-10).
- Legal to receive SOW draft and procurement checklist (Jordan).
- Schedule follow-up call week of 2026-03-15 to review pricing tiers and finalize forecast.
